title: Floating Hotel
context: Should Vancouver allow a 250-room floating hotel beside the Vancouver Convention Centre?
argumentFor: Adds hotel rooms and visitor-serving space beside the convention centre without using scarce downtown land, while creating a new public walkway.
argumentAgainst: Adds private commercial activity to the waterfront and could affect the harbour, public access, and the character of Vancouver's shoreline.

title: Lower Speed Limits
context: Should Vancouver lower speed limits on some streets including downtown?
argumentFor: Lowering speeds from 50 km/h to 40 or 30 reduces the severity of crashes and make streets safer for people walking, biking, and rolling.
argumentAgainst: Lower limits can lengthen trips, frustrate drivers, and may have limited effect without better street design and enforcement.

title: Renters Office
context: Should Vancouver fund a City-run office that helps renters understand their rights and navigate disputes?
argumentFor: Gives renters practical support in a tight housing market and makes tenant protections easier to understand and use.
argumentAgainst: The service cost roughly $600,000 a year and tenant advocacy should be provided by senior governments or community groups.

title: Beach Avenue Bike Lane
context: Should Vancouver keep an all-ages-and-abilities bike route on Beach Avenue between Hornby and Stanley Park?
argumentFor: The seperated bike route was added in 2020 and is heavily used. It provides a safe biking and walking route, and it doesn't make sense to spend money to remove it.
argumentAgainst: Removing the lane would restore two-way vehicle traffic and give drivers more direct access to Stanley Park.

title: Villages Plan
context: Should Vancouver turn 17 small commercial nodes into walkable, mixed-use neighbourhood hubs with more homes and shops?
argumentFor: Adds medium-density (up to 6-storeys) housing and everyday services in existing neighbourhood centres, making it easier to live near shops, jobs, and transit.
argumentAgainst: The scale and pace of change threaten neighbourhood character and might strain existing infrastructure.

title: Zero-Means-Zero Budget
context: Are you in favour of freezing property taxes at the current rate, while requiring the City to raise fees or cut programs?
argumentFor: Reduces tax burden for households and businesses and pushes the City to find efficiencies before asking taxpayers for more.
argumentAgainst: A tax freeze forces cuts to public services, eliminates municipal jobs, and raises user fees. The ever-increasing police budget would remain unaffected.

title: Elected Park Board
context: Do you think Vancouver should have an elected Park Board?
argumentFor: The Park Board is a unique and distinct voice for our public spaces. Eliminating it would concentrate more power over public spaces in City Council.
argumentAgainst: Abolishing the Park Board could simplify decision-making, reduce duplicated administration, and align parks with the rest of the city's services.

title: Safeway Towers
context: Should Vancouver approve three rental towers with more than 1,000 homes beside Commercial-Broadway Station?
argumentFor: Adds homes next to one of Vancouver's most connected transit nodes and keeps new housing close to shops and services.
argumentAgainst: The project's height and scale are disproportionate with the nearby buildings. Only 10% of units are allocated for below-market housing.

title: Bitcoin-Friendly City
context: Should Vancouver invest in Bitcoin and accept it for payment for business services?
argumentFor: Explores new payment and financial technology options and could position Vancouver as an innovation-friendly city.
argumentAgainst: Public money should not be exposed to a volatile asset, and Bitcoin may distract from more immediate city priorities.

title: Increased Police Budget
context: Should Vancouver spend more to expand the Vancouver Police Department, including hiring additional officers?
argumentFor: Adds police capacity for emergency response, investigations, and public safety in a growing city.
argumentAgainst: The police budget increased 44% between 2022 and 2026, taking money from housing, mental-health, and community services that may address the causes of harm more directly.

title: Natural Gas in New Builds
context: Should Vancouver allow new homes and buildings to use natural gas for heating and hot water?
argumentFor: Keeps more heating options available and may lower upfront costs for some new buildings and households.
argumentAgainst: Locks new buildings into fossil-fuel infrastructure, which makes it harder to reduce emissions. Also increases renovation costs for retrofits.

title: Downtown OPS
context: Should Vancouver allow a proposed overdose prevention site at 900 Helmcken Street?
argumentFor: Keeps people who use drugs alive and connects them with health care, treatment, and other supports in a high-need area.
argumentAgainst: Concerns about safety, street disorder, and whether the proposed location is appropriate for the surrounding community.
